props.title: Wedding Crashers

sections.content: Wedding Crashers (2005) revolutionized R-rated comedies in the 2000s, paving the way for hits like The Hangover (2009) and Bridesmaids (2011). Owen Wilson and Vince Vaughn's electric chemistry as divorce mediators who crash weddings to meet women captured lightning in a bottle. The film brilliantly balances raunchy humor with genuine heart, especially when John (Wilson) falls for Claire (Rachel McAdams). It marked a turning point away from the teen comedies of the late 90s toward more adult-oriented fare that could still deliver massive box office returns. The Hangover|2009|Three groomsmen lose their about-to-be-married buddy in Las Vegas and must retrace their wild night|Netflix Old School|2003|Three thirty-something friends attempt to recapture their college days by starting a fraternity|Paramount+ Bridesmaids|2011|A lovelorn and broke maid of honor struggles to fulfill her duties for her best friend's wedding|Prime Video

The mid-2000s saw a resurgence of ensemble comedies that mixed raunch with romance. Knocked Up (2007) and Superbad (2007) followed Wedding Crashers' template of combining crude humor with genuine emotional stakes. The film also revitalized the careers of Christopher Walken and Will Ferrell, whose scene-stealing cameo as Chazz showed how supporting characters could elevate these comedies beyond their premises.

Wedding Crashers' influence extends to its clever use of music, particularly with "Shout" becoming a wedding reception anthem. The film's success also helped establish Rachel McAdams as a leading actress, coming right after her breakout in Mean Girls (2004). Its quotable dialogue ("Ma! The meatloaf!") entered pop culture permanently, while its balance of heart and humor influenced countless romantic comedies that followed. Forgetting Sarah Marshall|2008|A heartbroken composer encounters his TV star ex-girlfriend at a Hawaiian resort|HBO Max I Love You, Man|2009|A friendless real estate agent seeks a best man for his upcoming wedding|Paramount+ Game Night|2018|A couples' game night spirals into a real criminal conspiracy|HBO Max SUBHEAD: The New Wave of Adult Comedy

Wedding Crashers' success sparked a renaissance in R-rated comedies that weren't afraid to mix sophisticated themes with outrageous situations. Films like The 40-Year-Old Virgin (2005) and Step Brothers (2008) followed suit, proving audiences would embrace comedies that balanced maturity with mayhem. The film's influence can still be seen in modern comedies like Crazy Rich Asians (2018), which similarly uses wedding culture as a backdrop for exploring relationships and family dynamics.
